name: rust-libbin-test-coverage
body:
source: the `libbin-fix` brief's test-coverage finding, extended by review `libbin-fix/feedback-2`. Gap: no test exercises either end of the module-prefix fix. The only Rust test fixture (`testdata/rust/fixture`) is lib-only and the only bin fixture in the tests is the frontend's own bin-only package, so neither the new collision nor the stability of the currently-scanning multi-target case is guarded.

Resolution (for the plan): two new fixtures under `testdata/rust/`, each driven by an e2e test through the fixture's scanner spool + the in-process ingestor (the `rust_frontend_records` pattern):

1. Collision case — `testdata/rust/libbin/`: a default lib+bin package, `[package] name = "foo"` with `src/lib.rs` (lib target `foo`) and `src/main.rs` (bin target `foo`), no explicit `[lib]`/`[[bin]]`. Assertion: `apg scan` completes without a duplicate-FQN panic, and the two crate roots render distinct module FQNs — each crate's units enumerate under its own prefix.

2. Stability case — `testdata/rust/libbin-distinct/`: a multi-target package with distinct target names, `[package] name = "foo"`, `[lib] name = "foo"`, `[[bin]] name = "foo-cli"`. This package scans today (distinct display names fall back to distinct prefixes `rust.foo` and `rust.foo-cli`). Assertion (regression): after the fix it renders exactly those module FQNs — `rust.foo` and `rust.foo-cli` — with no unit FQN renamed; pin the two FQN literals in the test so any drift fails loudly. This is the `requirements.constraint.rust-crate-fqn-stability` guarantee for a currently-scanning package.

`testdata/**` is excluded from a different change-set's decomposition scope, but both fixtures are required for this requirement. [autonomous]
